messages:
incidents-bot: ALERT: Elevated 500s observed on /v1/paging endpoints across canary region eu-west-1. Error spike started ~2024-11-08T14:20:30Z. Alerting oncall.

carla: seeing lots of aborted streaming sessions too. Paging cursor decode failures in logs: "invalid cursor version 0x05". This lines up with the sdk v5.2 rollout from this morning.

mike: confirmed. Canary traffic is 10% for sdk-v5.2. Error rate on that tag ~18% vs baseline 0.6%. Repro locally by calling the client with long cursor chain.

jen-sre: tagging this P0. Assigning oncall. @mike pls coordinate immediate mitigation. Do we have a feature-flag kill switch we can flip? :rotating_light:

mike: yes — feature flag name is `sdk_v5_paging_enabled`. Ops console shows flag controls runtime branching between cursor encodings. I can flip to false for canary.

sam: if we flip the flag, will it affect all customers or only rollout groups?

carla: it respects rollout groups. Turning to false for canary will send those requests to compatibility code path (v4 encoding). Should drop errors quickly.

mike: performing kill-switch now (doing a staged flip for eu-west-1 canary group)...


deploy-bot: FLAG_CHANGE: `sdk_v5_paging_enabled` set to false for rollout-group "canary-eu-west-1" by mike at 2024-11-08T14:23:15Z.

carla: monitoring logs... error rate falling. 500s down to 2.7% in last 60s. Streaming aborts still present for a subset of requests — likely cached clients with bad cursors.

jen-sre: good. Triggering rollback of the canary deployment too. We should fully revert the sdk-v5 artifact in canary and promote the fallback. @deploy-bot can you start canary rollback?

deploy-bot: ROLLBACK_INIT: rolling back deployment canary-svc@eu-west-1 from image sdk-v5.2 -> sdk-v5.1 at 2024-11-08T14:25:04Z. Estimated completion ~2m.

mike: starting a quick mitigation checklist — posting for handoff: 1) Flag off for canary (done), 2) rollback canary (in progress), 3) route canary traffic to v4-compatible model if needed, 4) add temporary note to status page if customers impacted, 5) begin customer impact triage.

lina-support: support triage: two paying customers reported stream disconnects and partial results. CS already opened tickets with request IDs. I'll prepare an interim message acknowledging and saying we're rolling back a canary.

carla: logs show ~1400 distinct request IDs failed in the last 10m, roughly 0.02% of total qps but concentrated for users on latest sdk. Might degrade UX for streaming-heavy apps.

jen-sre: agree we should keep the incident open until rollback completes and we see 95th p50 latencies back to normal. @mike @carla handoff to oncall shift — I'll step out for the next 30m, ping me if rollback doesn't finish.

mike: will monitor and update here. If rollback completes but errors persist, plan B: forced route fallback at edge (route-table) to ensure no v5 cursor parsing attempted.

deploy-bot: ROLLBACK_COMPLETE: canary-svc@eu-west-1 rollback to sdk-v5.1 completed at 2024-11-08T14:27:02Z.

carla: seeing residual errors but trending down. 500s at 0.3% now. Streaming aborts almost gone.

mike: verifying client compatibility: looks like new cursor header format introduced in v5.2 used a non-backwards-compatible variant when clients had long cursor chains. We'll ship a patch to accept both encodings in server within 2 hours, but release cadence for SDK fix will be separate.

lina-support: outgoing note drafted for affected customers: "We've reverted a canary release impacting streaming/paging for clients on SDK v5.2. If you saw aborted streams, try reinitializing cursors. Engineering is rolling a server-side mitigation and we'll publish a follow-up."

jen-sre: good. For postmortem, capture root cause (cursor encoding bump + insufficient canary checks), timeline, mitigations (flag kill, canary rollback), customer impact (list of ticket IDs), and recommended actions (contract compatibility testing + forced compatibility tests in CI). Assigning postmortem owner: carla.

mike: creating follow-up task to add backward-compatible decode in runtime, add canary traffic fuzz tests for paging, and expand the canary watch window.

incidents-bot: INCIDENT_UPDATE: Severity P0 -> P1 at 2024-11-08T14:31:38Z after rollback and error rates stabilized.

carla: handing off to next oncall @jen-sre for continued monitoring. I'll assemble the timeline and customer impact notes.

jen-sre: taking it. If anything spikes again, escalate to eng-runtime and product. Closing active mitigation channel in 30m if stable. :white_check_mark:
